newsitem.title: USA: Checkpoint, Ultrak stocks down after merger canceled.
newsitem.headline: Checkpoint, Ultrak stocks down after merger canceled.

text.p: Shares of Checkpoint Systems Inc. and Ultrak Inc. fell sharply Friday after the two makers of security systems cancelled a $397 million merger agreement and projected lower earnings.
Checkpoint plummeted $7.125, or more than 41 percent, to $10 on the New York Stock Exchange, where it was the most actively traded stock and suffered the biggest percentage loss.
Ultrak fell $5, or 30 percent, to $11.50 on Nasdaq, where it was the second-biggest percentage loser.

Thorofare, N.J.-based Checkpoint said Thursday it and Ultrak, based in Carrollton, Texas, cancelled their merger pact by mutual consent. It said the main reason for the termination was perceived "channel conflict" with Ultrak's distribution network.
Under terms of the pact, each Ultrak share would have been exchanged for 1.15 Checkpoint shares.
Checkpoint makes securities and surveillance products for retailers, and Ultrak makes and services closed-circuit television and related products for use in security and surveillance operations.

Checkpoint said its earnings and revenues for the first quarter and for 1997 would not meet analysts' expectations. It said a combination of foreign currency fluctuations, the timing of some significant orders, and a one-time charge relating to Ultrak merger expenses would result in first-quarter revenue of about $68 million and earnings per share of about 7 cents, below what it said were analysts' estimates of 16 cents.
The company also estimated that for 1997, it will report revenues of about $325 million and earnings of about 67 cents per share, compared with estimates of 90 cents.

Ultrak also warned of weaker results. It said it expected earnings from operations to equal 16 cents to 18 cents a share, not including a three cents per share non-recurring expense associated with the termination of its merger with Checkpoint.

Wall Street's consensus earnings estimate for Ultrak, according to First Call, which tracks analysts' earnings projections, for the first quarter was 21 cents a share, versus 16 cents a share earned in the year-ago quarter. On Feb. 19, the company had said it was "comfortable" with such estimates.
Ultrak said it expected first-quarter revenues of about $42 million, versus $30 million in the same quarter last year.
